extracted.intended_audience: attorneys admitted to practice before the USPTO; respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings; OED/USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 following a state suspension, setting forth suspension terms, probation, limited recognition, procedures for noncompliance, publication, and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24; a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24' was sent notifying Respondent that the OED Director filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24' requesting identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service of the Notice and Order (certified mail) and delivery to Respondent were documented. Where Respondent fails to file a response, there is 'no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)' and reciprocal suspension followed by probation is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension term
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for one (1) year and one (1) day, with all but sixty (60) days deferred, effective the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The active suspension period is sixty (60) days; the remainder of the one-year-and-one-day term is deferred consistent with the underlying state order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reinstatement (§11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.60 after the sixty-day suspension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice in trademark and non-patent matters before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to §11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with §11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed, and expiring thirty (30) days after the date the Final Order is signed, with such limited recognition being granted for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is temporary (30 days) and narrowly confined to actions necessary to comply with §11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.58
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly requires compliance with the rule; limited recognition is provided to enable that compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation period
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a 2-year unsupervised probationary period commencing on the date of reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The probationary period mirrors the discipline ordered by the Supreme Court of Louisiana and begins upon reinstatement to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be permitted to practice before the USPTO in the practice of trademark and other non-patent law during her probationary period, unless her probation is revoked and she is suspended by order of the USPTO Director or otherwise no longer has the authority to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permission to practice during probation is conditional and may be curtailed if probation is revoked or other authority to practice is lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director procedure for alleged probationary noncompliance — Order to Show Cause (initial)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of this Final Order or any provision of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, the OED Director shall: (A) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not enter an order immediately suspending the Respondent for up to one additional year for the violations set forth in the Final Order; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record Respondent furnished to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.11(a); and (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure requires issuance of an Order to Show Cause, service to the last address on record per §11.11(a), and a 15-day response period.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director procedure after response period — referral to USPTO Director
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) If after the 15-day period for response and consideration of the response, if any, the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall: (A) deliver to the USPTO Director or his designee: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response to the Order to Show Cause, if any, and (iii) argument and evidence supporting the OED Director's position; and (B) request that the USPTO Director enter an order suspending Respondent from practice before the USPTO for up to one additional year for the violations set forth in the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If OED remains of the opinion of noncompliance after considering any response, it must forward the record and request additional suspension from the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to seek discrete discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing therein shall prevent the OED Director from seeking discrete discipline for any misconduct that formed the basis for an Order to Show Cause issued pursuant to paragraph '8'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED may pursue separate disciplinary actions for misconduct underlying the Order to Show Cause, in addition to procedures under this Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review does not stay enforcement action
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the Respondent seeks a review of any action taken pursuant to paragraph '8', such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance such action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or judicial review of enforcement actions does not automatically stay or delay the action taken under the Order to Show Cause procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' text describing the suspension, underlying state proceedings, the terms of suspension and probation, and that Ms. Lenise R. Williams is not authorized to practice before the Office in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order prescribes the content and material consistency of the public notice; the sample notice text is included in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (§11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires dissemination of discipline information to relevant state disciplinary authorities, courts of admission, and public notice channels per §11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Respondent's failure to respond to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has not filed a response to the Notice and Order. In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and Respondent's suspension, followed by probation, is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to a §11.24 Notice and Order can result in a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists and the imposition of reciprocal discipline without contested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction: not authorized to practice in patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Suspension states: 'Ms. Lenise R. Williams is not authorized to practice before the Office in patent matters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly addresses and records current non-authorization to practice patent matters as part of the public notice.
